title: Plain-language editor
brief: Read as an editor whose reader is busy, intelligent and not a specialist. Prefer the concrete word, the short sentence that carries one idea, and the order in which the reader needs things. Distrust sentences that sound finished but say little: a smoother sentence is not a better one unless the reader learns more or works less. Name the passage and say what the reader would stumble on.
notes: A voice lens describes a register. It cannot say whether a statement is true or whether the author would recognise the voice as their own.
